scope: Actual local Flutter UI. Product fixture is a dated public Maggi catalogue report and its sourced Open Food Facts image. Camera uses an owned synthetic label fixture; no physical camera or account provider is exercised.

baseline_comparison.reason: Earlier before captures used a synthetic report; final captures use the public Maggi report. Their structure can be reviewed, but this is not a matched-content pixel comparison.

reference_acceptance: Responsive hierarchy and latest smaller phone typography were visually reviewed. No exact pixel-equivalence claim.

typography.source: Existing bundled licensed fonts. Screenshot review and actual-font widget geometry; Flutter canvas font loading is not inferred from DOM computed styles.

behaviors: The unchanged application paints the sourced Maggi photo in WebKit 26 with test-only CanvasKit software rendering. Default Windows headless GPU mode leaves it blank. Both engines receive the identical valid JPEG with CORS allowed; native HTMLImage.decode succeeds inWebKit. No global software renderer or application workaround was added.

spacing.limits: Flutter draws cards on canvas. DOM semantics measure visible bounds and scroll clipping; they do not establish actual card padding, column gaps or a valid layout score.
spacing.input_projection: The measurement submission retained all captured element geometry, labels, parent identity and spacing properties; nonspacing presentation styles and redundant client/scroll metrics were omitted from the tool payload. Full original captures remain in raw_states.

remaining_limits: Default Windows headless WebKit GPU mode leaves the remote photo blank; the unchanged application paints it under test-only CanvasKitCPU. PhysicaliPhoneSafariGPU/image acceptance remains unverified. No globalCPU forcing or app performance regression was introduced.
No physical iPhone Safari camera permission, sensor framing, browser toolbar/keyboard, Google consent or LiveContainer acceptance.
Reduced-motion render/reachability checks are not a real-device scrolling or animation frame-rate benchmark.
Local browser rendering does not establish hosted deployment or native publication.

remote_image_diagnosis.comparison: Identical JPEG bytes and successful native HTML decode rule out a missing source, CORS rejection or invalid image. The pinned Flutter engine uses an HTMLImage lazy GPU texture on WebKit. Switching only the test bootstrap to CanvasKit CPU makes the image visible in the unchanged application.
remote_image_diagnosis.software_configuration: canvasKitForceCpuOnly:true injected by a local Playwright route; no application bootstrap/source change.
remote_image_diagnosis.limits: This isolates the local Windows WebKit GPU path; it does not establish a failure or acceptance on physical iPhone Safari.
